definition_used: When a journal/publisher/institution states that one or more company(ies)/institution(s)/thirdparty(ies) have not met the journal/publisher/institution’s standards of publishing and/or research ethics. RW will use this reason when no other information about the correction/EOC/retraction is available (i.e., the notice only states that there was an ethical violation), or when the ethical violation (as an additional reason) cannot be addressed by existing reasons.
caution: The definition is a catch-all for ethical violations by non-author entities when details are unavailable. It signals an investigation by journal/publisher/institution into a company/institution/third party, but the specific ethical breach is unspecified. This makes it a broad governance and transparency signal rather than a direct indicator of research content reliability or authorship integrity. Main figure not recommended due to opacity and lack of specific content-related problem.
semantic_rationale: The reason indicates a journal/publisher/institution finding that a company/institution/third party violated publishing/research ethics standards. It is used when no further details are available, making it a notice of an ethical breach by a non-author entity. This maps to editorial_peer_review_governance (publisher enforcement of standards) and post_publication_transparency_due_process_oversight (opaque notice of an investigation). The problem object is article_general because the specific issue is unknown. Process signals include journal_publisher_investigation, institutional_investigation, third_party_investigation, and notice_opacity. Actor context includes company_institution, third_party, and journal_publisher as the investigating body.
